item.title: Book Club: Happy Iceland — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Six: FEB 16, 2027 Happy Iceland, Anne Marie Wells, 2026 Non-fiction/Memoir Part memoir, part travel narrative, Anne Marie Wells reflects on her experiences living in and exploring Iceland. Through personal stories, cultural observations, and encounters with Icelanders, she offers an affectionate portrait of contemporary Icelandic life.

item.title: Book Club: Animal Life — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Four: DEC 15, 2026 Animal Life, Auður Ava Ólafsdóttir, 2022 Fiction During a snowy Christmas season in Reykjavík, a lonely middle-aged woman unexpectedly becomes connected to a young pregnant immigrant and her child. A tender and often humorous novel about family, belonging, aging, and human connection.

item.title: Book Club: In Valhalla’s Shadows — Icelandic Canadian Club of Toronto
item.description:
Session Three: NOV 17, 2026 In Valhalla’s Shadows, W.D. Valgardson, 2019 Mystery/Noir Set in Manitoba’s Icelandic community, this atmospheric mystery follows a retired police officer investigating a decades-old disappearance. Valgardson combines Nordic noir elements with prairie history, memory, family secrets, and questions of identity.

item.title: ICELANDERS OF SPRING RIDGE — Icelandic Roots
item.description: By Fred Bjarnason Victoria, British Columbia, was a very different place when Icelanders began to settle here in 1883 than it is now. The city followed the waterfront along the inner harbour, extending inland only about four or five blocks. The Icelanders began to settle in an area east of the main city known as Spring Ridge, now the neighbour of Fernwood.
